analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: China Gets A Boost, Tech Jitters Linger As Rates Stay Quiet
key_insights: Chinese equities rose in the Asia session after reports the financial regulator met banks and securities firms on measures to support capital markets. Cailian reported the meeting will study optimising lending programmes for stock buybacks, and a major state-owned bank reportedly plans to raise lending quotas to asset managers for stock purchases. Shenzhen Composite +1.92% and China H shares +0.67% as at 0710 GMT.

Kioxia fell just under 16% in Tokyo after a cautious outlook, adding to worries around parts of the AI sector. The Nikkei was down 0.33%. The author notes moves of 10% or more have become more common over the past week and does not view this as healthy.
Nasdaq was up 0.8% in early Monday trade after a 2.86% fall on Friday, so the Kioxia news had little effect on it.
US rates were quiet overnight. Volumes returned to recent averages, with 130k TY traded in the overnight session and no clear flow pattern. The larger call buying seen on Friday was absent.
Friday's rates options flow: paper paid from 9.5 up to 11 for 50k FVF7 107 calls, and Week 1 TY 107.75 calls were bought for 7 in 50k.
Alphabet is conducting a seven-part Euro bond offering, including 4y, 6y, 9y, 13y and 19y tenors. Its previous Euro offering raised EUR 9 bn.

Central banks and Treasury supply drive the week: quarterly borrowing estimates Monday, RBA Tuesday, quarterly refunding announcement Wednesday, BoE Thursday. UBS expects the US Treasury to leave auction sizes unchanged this quarter and to prepare markets for supply adjustments from May 2027.

Markets price 21bp of hikes for the RBA meeting. Cotality data show Australian house prices fell for a seventh straight month, on track for the largest drop in 40 years. The major-cities Home Value Index fell 1.7% in October and is down 8.1% over seven months.

Unions criticised last week's UK Budget, warning Chancellor Healey against 'a trade-off between jobs and wages' after he declined to recommit to a 2024 manifesto pledge to end 'discriminatory age bands'.

Ryanair said it must cut costs across the group to offset a $2 bn increase in fuel charges next year, including reviewing airport deals, possibly cutting crew on flights and using more AI. First-half net profit fell 15% and fares fell in the first half, with the US-Iran war making consumers hesitant.

The final NYT/Siena poll shows Democrats ahead in the seven key states most likely to decide Senate control, with the largest gains in Maine and Michigan. The lead is said to be large enough to win the Senate even if polls underestimate Republicans as much as in 2016 or 2020.

The Financial Times found US stocks have risen in the six months after midterms for more than 70 years, the last decline being 1946. US stocks have never been this expensive heading into midterms. Carson Investment notes the S&P 500 has averaged 13.7% annual return under a Republican president with a split Congress since 1951, versus 4.9% when Democrats control both the House and Senate.
